items.q:
Every time you change one line of app code, this build reinstalls all pip packages. Which reorder fixes it?

FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
options: COPY requirements.txt first, RUN pip install, then COPY . .
Put RUN pip install before FROM
items.explain: Layers are cached top-down until the first changed layer, so copy only requirements.txt before the install and the app code after it.

items.q:
The app listens on port 8000 inside the container. You run:

docker run -d -p 5000:8000 myapp

Which URL reaches it from the host machine?
items.explain: -p HOST:CONTAINER maps host port 5000 to container port 8000; EXPOSE is documentation only and does not publish anything.

items.q: You run docker run postgres three times. How many images and how many containers exist now?
items.explain: An image is a read-only template pulled once; each run creates a separate container from it.

items.q: A Postgres container stores data at /var/lib/postgresql/data. After docker rm and a new docker run, the tables are gone. Which flag would have kept them?
items.explain: A container's writable layer is deleted with the container; a named volume mounted at the data path lives outside it.

items.q: What is the difference between RUN and CMD in a Dockerfile?
options: RUN runs at build time; CMD is the container's start command
RUN is for Linux, CMD is for Windows images
CMD executes at build time; RUN runs when the container starts
They are the same, CMD is the older spelling
items.explain: RUN creates a new image layer during build (install packages), while CMD is stored and executed only when a container starts.

items.q:
In this compose file the web service cannot reach the database using localhost:5432. What hostname should DATABASE_URL use?

services:
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://u:p@localhost:5432/app
  db:
    image: postgres:16
items.explain: Each service is its own container; compose puts them on a shared network where the service name is the DNS hostname.

items.q: A container starts and exits immediately. docker ps shows nothing. Which command shows why?
items.explain: Logs from a stopped container are still stored (use docker ps -a to find its id); exec cannot attach to a container that is not running.

items.q: Which Dockerfile produces a smaller final image for a compiled Go or Java app?
options: One stage that installs the compiler and builds the app
A multi-stage build copying only the binary into a slim image
A single stage with apt-get clean at the end
Any Dockerfile, as long as you use docker image prune
items.explain: Multi-stage builds leave the compiler and source in a throwaway stage and ship only the output in the final image.

items.q: You mount your source folder with -v $(pwd):/app for live reload, but a file named node_modules from the host overwrites the container's install. What is the usual fix?
options: Delete node_modules on the host permanently
Run docker commit after every change
items.explain: A more specific mount at /app/node_modules shadows that sub-path, so the container keeps its own installed dependencies.

items.q: What does docker compose down -v do that docker compose down does not?
options: Also removes the named volumes declared in the compose file
Stops containers but keeps their networks
items.explain: -v removes volumes, so database data created by the stack is deleted; plain down keeps volumes for the next up.

items.q: Build A: FROM python:3.12, RUN pip install fastapi, COPY app.py . Build B: same but you changed a comment in app.py only. Which layers are rebuilt in B?
options: None, the cache is reused fully
items.explain: The cache is valid up to the first instruction whose input changed; FROM and RUN are unchanged, so only COPY (and anything after it) reruns.
